---
title: "Install the advanced source workflow"
---

::: {.callout-note}
For ordinary Python use or the installed `metis train` Hydra interface, start
with the [package quickstart](../package/quickstart.qmd). That workflow supports
CPU training and saves portable artifacts. Both pip and uv are supported.

This page covers the historical `train.py` workflow in a source checkout. It
exposes advanced CUDA/DDP and sequence-conditioning settings, requires a
compatible CUDA PyTorch installation and NVIDIA GPU, and uses a different
checkpoint format.
:::

## Set up a source checkout

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Git, then run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git
cd metis
uv sync --extra legacy
```

The `legacy` extra supplies the historical trainer's plotting, terminal and
Weights & Biases dependencies. Base-package installation alone does not supply
them. Check that your PyTorch build and GPU driver are compatible before using
this trainer; installing dependencies does not configure GPU drivers.

Keep the extra explicit when running historical recipes:

```bash
uv run --extra legacy train.py --config-name default
```

For the Python dependencies used by the historical notebooks and documentation,
include the `docs` extra too:

```bash
uv sync --extra legacy --extra docs
```

Use the resulting environment in your notebook interface. The Quarto CLI is a
separate system installation; the `docs` extra does not install it. These
dependencies also do not make historical CUDA training cells run on CPU.

## Develop and run tests

uv includes the development dependency group by default. Include the pandas
extra to exercise the optional pandas adapter tests as well as the legacy
compatibility tests:

```bash
uv sync --extra legacy --extra pandas
uv run --extra legacy --extra pandas pytest -v
uv run ty check src
uv run ruff check src tests
```

The automated numerical test suite runs on CPU. Passing those tests does not
establish GPU compatibility or scientific accuracy. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the build, installed-wheel checks and documentation workflow.
